justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `SubstanceSourceMaterial` in base R6 as a deprecated transitional resource while adding `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances but leaves parallel source-material representations and continued maintenance of a draft/FMM 0 model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, consolidating immature R4 substance source-material content into the R6 `SubstanceDefinition` model, is reasonable. R4 `SubstanceSourceMaterial` was trial-use/FMM 0, and the R6 package retains a source-material concept only inside `SubstanceDefinition`, so the compatibility obligation is lower than for a mature resource. The breakage is still substantial, but the less-breaking base option would materially undermine the cleanup by preserving a second resource identity for the same domain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `SubstanceSourceMaterial` as a deprecated R6 resource for one or more releases while introducing `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. That would let existing R4 instances, generated classes, validators, and endpoints continue to work. This is only a partial alternative because it creates two core ways to represent source-material facts, risks permanent accumulation of deprecated resource shapes, and requires validators, search, examples, and implementer guidance to support both models. Conversion tooling or an external cross-version map would help migration, but those are mitigations rather than a backward-compatible base R6 design.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Carry forward the detailed R4 source-material fields in base R6, either on a deprecated resource or as optional details under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves lossless migration but carries a broad low-maturity content model into R6 and can duplicate or confuse the simplified source-material representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The compact R6 `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial` shape suggests a reasonable goal of simplifying and integrating source-material data. However, the local evidence does not show an official rationale or destinations for many R4 details such as fractions, organism identifiers, hybrid data, detailed taxonomy, parent substances, and part locations. Without that design record, the reasonableness of losing this much base-model fidelity cannot be judged confidently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have preserved the old detail model as optional deprecated elements, either by retaining the old resource or by adding the detailed children under `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial`. That would cover more R4-valid content and reduce data-loss pressure during migration. It is only partial because it would keep a large immature structure in the core model, may overlap with other `SubstanceDefinition` elements, and could leave implementers with both compact and detailed same-domain representations indefinitely. Standard extensions or conversion maps can mitigate loss, but they do not by themselves make base R6 backward compatible.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use an extensible rather than required binding for `SubstanceDefinition.sourceMaterial.countryOfOrigin`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Accepts more legacy R4 codings and text, but weakens the R6 guarantee that country of origin is drawn from the common country ValueSet.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing a country-of-origin element on the common FHIR country ValueSet is a reasonable interoperability goal, and required binding is defensible for a field whose semantics are specifically country or jurisdiction codes. The breakage is limited to migrated values that used local codes, free text, historical labels, or non-country concepts. A less-breaking binding strength exists, but it would not deliver the same strict conformance guarantee.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would be to make the R6 binding extensible, preserving more R4-valid `CodeableConcept` values while still encouraging ISO country codes. This is a partial alternative because extensible binding would permit divergent local codings when implementations claim no suitable ValueSet code, reducing consistent validation and downstream comparability. A published ConceptMap or normalization table would be valuable migration guidance, but it is not itself a backward-compatible base-design alternative.
